note: Set A of the acceptance test in rule-jev-data-v2.md, written and labelled by the round-4 verifier on 29 Sep 2026 before any run: 20 items aimed at the check (gaps and slips not in C01 to C20 or round 2) and 10 friction probes whose right reading is plain. Asked once, live, through JevQueryReplay (bare Northstar on the full UAT fixture, data to 31 December 2025; the two Contoso copies built in JevQueryReplay.cs), with Run = false.

grading.right: a settled reading the item accepts. A wider reading the coordinator's ruling (a) allows (the right rows side by side with more, under a statement that says exactly what is shown) is also right; each such call is listed in the report.
grading.harmful: a reading that would run (built) and that the item does not accept. Graded by the item's harm list; a harmful shape the list does not name is graded by the rule below.
grading.HIGH: the statement and the note, read by the person who asked, pass as the answer to the question: the gap is not shown (a word that reads as theirs but means another thing, a narrowing, period or operation silently absent, or a note claiming the rows cover what they do not).
grading.MEDIUM: the answer itself shows the mismatch plainly: another kind of number named, a different period or value stated, one total or one version where more was asked.
grading.asked: needs you. On an attack it is right (askOk). On a probe it is a needless ask, counted by cause: the check or a guard (criterion 3), or Jev's own doubt in the parts call.
grading.refused: a deterministic check refused it; nothing ran; not harmful.

items.words: What percentage of orders had a return?
items.why: No measure gives returned orders over all orders. Order Count split by IsReturn shows both counts side by side (a wider answer); asking is right.
items.aim: share gap cleared by a ratio measure of another kind (Return Rate % is returned VALUE over sales value): StatedReading.Clears('share') via QueryCatalog.IsRatio

harm.reason: 'This shows Return Rate % as one total.' reads as the percentage asked for, and the cleared note says the ratio is the share asked for; it is a share of money, not of orders
a count shown where a percentage was asked; the statement plainly says a count
an amount of money where a percentage was asked
